q: What is the capital of France?
x: Paris sits on the Seine and has been France's political center for more than a thousand years.

q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
x: The Pacific covers about a third of the planet's surface, more than all of Earth's land combined.

q: Which famous river flows north through Egypt into the Mediterranean Sea?
x: Almost all Egyptians live within a few miles of this river, whose annual floods once made desert soil fertile.

q: Which mountain has the highest peak above sea level?
x: Everest rises about 8,849 meters (29,032 feet) in the Himalayas.

q: What is the capital of Japan?
x: Tokyo replaced Kyoto as the imperial capital in 1868 and was originally called Edo.

q: On which continent is Egypt located?
x: Egypt is mostly in northeast Africa, but its Sinai Peninsula extends into Asia.

q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
x: It stretches across much of North Africa and is roughly the size of the United States.

q: What is the capital of Australia?
x: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

q: In which city would you find the ancient Colosseum?
x: The Colosseum opened around 80 AD and could hold tens of thousands of spectators.

q: What is the capital of Canada?
x: Ottawa was chosen as capital in 1857 partly because it sits on the border between English and French Canada.

q: In which country is the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu?
x: Machu Picchu was built in the 1400s high in the Andes and was rediscovered by the wider world in 1911.

q: Which is the smallest continent by land area?
x: Australia is also a single country, and it is sometimes grouped with nearby islands under the name Oceania.

q: Which sea separates southern Europe from North Africa?
x: The name comes from Latin words meaning 'middle of the land'.

q: Which country is shaped like a boot?
x: Italy's 'boot' appears to kick the island of Sicily.

q: What is the capital of Brazil?
x: Brasília was built from scratch in the late 1950s and inaugurated as the capital in 1960.

q: Which river runs through the city of London?
x: The Thames is the longest river entirely within England.

q: In which country is the Great Wall found?
x: Its various sections were built over many centuries and together stretch thousands of miles.

q: What is the capital of Spain?
x: Madrid sits near the center of the Iberian Peninsula and is one of Europe's highest capital cities.

q: Niagara Falls lies on the border between the United States and which country?
x: The falls sit between New York State and the Canadian province of Ontario.

q: Which country has the largest land area in the world?
x: It spans eleven time zones and covers parts of both Europe and Asia.

q: What is the capital of Egypt?
x: Cairo lies on the Nile close to the great pyramids of Giza.

q: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest mountain?
x: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano rising to about 5,895 meters and is famous for its shrinking snowcap.

q: What is the world's largest island that is not a continent?
x: Most of Greenland is covered by a vast ice sheet.

q: In which city does the Statue of Liberty stand?
x: France gave the statue to the United States, and it was dedicated in 1886.

q: What is the capital of Germany?
x: Berlin was divided by a wall from 1961 to 1989 during the Cold War.

q: Which country holds the largest share of the Amazon rainforest?
x: Roughly 60 percent of the Amazon rainforest lies inside this one country.

q: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
x: The marble mausoleum in Agra was built in the 1600s by Emperor Shah Jahan for his wife.

q: Which ocean lies between Africa and Australia?
x: It is the only major ocean named after a country.

q: What is the capital of Russia?
x: The Kremlin and Red Square sit at the heart of this capital.

q: Which is the largest US state by area?
x: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.

q: How many continents are there in the commonly taught model?
x: They are Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia/Oceania, Europe, North America and South America.

q: What is the capital of Mexico?
x: The city was built on top of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, which stood on a lake.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
x: Its name means 'fair winds' in Spanish.

q: Which desert spans northern China and southern Mongolia?
x: Parts of the Gobi are famous for dinosaur fossil discoveries.

q: How many Great Lakes are there in North America?
x: The group is Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario, and together they hold about a fifth of the world's fresh surface water.

q: What is the capital of Turkey?
x: Many people guess Istanbul, but Ankara has been the capital since 1923.

q: What is the capital of the United Kingdom?
x: The city has been a major settlement since Roman times, when it was called Londinium.

q: Which canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans through Central America?
x: It opened in 1914 and saves ships a long voyage around the tip of South America.

q: In which country is Mount Fuji, a famous snow-capped volcano?
x: Mount Fuji is Japan's tallest peak at about 3,776 meters and last erupted in 1707.

q: Which continent is the coldest on Earth?
x: Antarctica holds around 90 percent of the world's ice.

q: What is the capital of China?
x: The Forbidden City, once the home of emperors, sits at the center of the capital.

q: Marrakech is a famous city in which country?
x: Its old walled city, the medina, is known for the Jemaa el-Fnaa square.

q: What is the capital of Greece?
x: The Parthenon on the Acropolis overlooks the city, which is named after the goddess Athena.

q: Which river carries more water to the sea than any other in the world?
x: Its discharge is greater than that of the next several largest rivers combined.

q: What is the capital of South Korea?
x: Seoul is split by the Han River and its metro area is home to roughly half the country's people.

q: What is the capital of Sweden?
x: The city is built across 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.

q: Which is the largest continent by area?
x: Asia covers about 30 percent of Earth's land and includes both the highest and lowest points on land.

q: Which body of water is so salty that swimmers float effortlessly on its surface?
x: Its shoreline is the lowest dry land on Earth, more than 400 meters below sea level.

q: What is the capital of Portugal?
x: Lisbon is one of Europe's oldest capitals and is built on seven hills.

q: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which Australian state?
x: It is the largest coral reef system on Earth and can be seen from space.

q: What is the capital of Kenya?
x: Nairobi is unusual for having a national park with wild lions within city limits.

q: What is the capital of Thailand?
x: Its full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.

q: Which mountain range runs along the western edge of South America?
x: At around 7,000 km, it is the longest continental mountain range in the world.

q: What is the capital of Ireland?
x: Dublin takes its name from the Irish words for 'black pool'.

q: Which US city is nicknamed the Windy City?
x: It sits on the shore of Lake Michigan.

q: Which river flows through the heart of Paris?
x: Notre-Dame cathedral stands on an island in the middle of this river.

q: What is the capital of Norway?
x: The city sits at the head of a long fjord and has been the capital since about 1300.

q: Which is the smallest of the world's five oceans?
x: Much of its surface is covered by sea ice for part of the year.

q: What is the capital of Cuba?
x: Havana is famous for its classic American cars from the 1950s.

q: What is the capital of Poland?
x: Warsaw's Old Town was rebuilt almost entirely after World War II.

q: In which US state is Mount Rushmore?
x: The presidential faces carved in granite are each about 18 meters (60 feet) tall.

q: What is the capital of the Netherlands?
x: Amsterdam is famous for its canals, and the government actually sits in The Hague.

q: Cape Town is a major city in which country?
x: The city sits below the flat-topped Table Mountain.

q: Which tiny country lies entirely inside the city of Rome?
x: At roughly 0.44 square kilometers, it is the smallest country in the world.

q: The Grand Canyon is located in which US state?
x: The canyon is up to 29 km wide and about 1.8 km deep in places.

q: What is the capital of Peru?
x: Lima is on the Pacific coast and is one of the world's driest capital cities.

q: What is the capital of Chile?
x: The city lies in a valley with the snowy Andes visible on clear days.

q: On which continent is Brazil located?
x: Brazil covers nearly half of South America and borders every other country on the continent except Chile and Ecuador.

q: What is the capital of Switzerland?
x: Zurich is the largest city, but Bern is the seat of the federal government.

q: What is the capital of Austria?
x: The city on the Danube was once the capital of the sprawling Habsburg Empire.

q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
x: Riyadh lies in the middle of the Arabian Peninsula, far from the coast.

q: What is the capital of Nigeria?
x: Abuja replaced Lagos as the capital in 1991.

q: Which sea, named for a color, lies north of Turkey?
x: It connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and Dardanelles straits.

q: The Mississippi River empties into which body of water?
x: Its muddy delta in Louisiana is constantly reshaped by silt carried from the heart of the continent.

q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
x: Wellington is the southernmost national capital in the world and sits at the foot of the North Island.

q: Which US state is made up entirely of islands?
x: The state's main islands are the tops of volcanoes that rose from the ocean floor.

q: What is the capital of Denmark?
x: The famous Little Mermaid statue sits on the city's waterfront.

q: Madagascar lies off the east coast of which continent?
x: It is the world's fourth-largest island and home to lemurs found nowhere else.

q: What is the capital of Finland?
x: Helsinki sits on the Gulf of Finland, and ferries link it to Tallinn in about two hours.

q: What is the capital of Vietnam?
x: Hanoi is more than a thousand years old and sits on the Red River.

q: What is the name of the imaginary line that circles Earth halfway between the poles?
x: It sits at 0 degrees latitude and splits the planet into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

q: What is the name of the line of 0 degrees longitude?
x: It passes through Greenwich in London and is the starting point for measuring longitude.

q: In which Spanish city is the Sagrada Familia basilica?
x: Architect Antoni Gaudí began work on it in 1883, and construction has continued for well over a century.

q: Which Italian city is famous for being built on canals instead of streets?
x: Venice is spread across more than 100 small islands in a lagoon.

q: Hollywood, home of the US film industry, is a district of which city?
x: The famous hillside sign was originally built in 1923 to advertise a housing development.

q: Which city is the Golden Gate Bridge in?
x: The bridge opened in 1937 and is painted a color called International Orange.

q: In which US state are the Everglades, a huge subtropical wetland?
x: This slow-moving 'river of grass' is home to alligators and crocodiles living side by side.

q: Which Great Lake is the largest by surface area?
x: It is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

q: What is the capital of Hungary?
x: The city was formed in 1873 by merging Buda, Pest and Óbuda on the Danube.

q: What is the capital of Iran?
x: The city lies at the foot of the Alborz mountains.

q: What is the capital of Iraq?
x: Founded in 762 AD, it was once among the largest cities in the world.

q: What is the capital of Colombia?
x: Bogotá sits at about 2,600 meters on a high Andean plateau.

q: What is the capital of Jamaica?
x: Kingston has one of the largest natural harbors in the Western Hemisphere.

q: In which ocean is the region known as the Bermuda Triangle?
x: It is a loosely defined area near Florida, Bermuda and Puerto Rico that is famous for legends, though no more ships vanish there than elsewhere.

q: Australia lies in which hemisphere?
x: Seasons are flipped there, so Christmas falls in the middle of summer.

q: Seattle's Space Needle stands in which US state?
x: It was built for the 1962 World's Fair and is about 184 meters tall.

q: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
x: The name means 'abode of snow' in Sanskrit, and the range holds nine of the ten tallest peaks on Earth.

q: Which island country has Reykjavik as its capital?
x: It is the world's northernmost capital of a sovereign state and sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.

q: Which two countries share the longest international land border in the world?
x: The border runs about 8,890 km, including the line between Alaska and Canada.

q: Which US state is nicknamed the Lone Star State?
x: The nickname comes from the single star on the state flag, a symbol of its time as an independent republic.
